label: Late original phase / <DEL> when the sequence started with w, m (or k)
explanation: A sustained-memory feature. It fires from the 4th original input (t>=3) through the <DEL> step, and almost never at t<=2 or during the copy phase (only 2% of mass, mostly at recall_idx 1). The input token at the current step barely matters. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends mainly on what the sequence started with: first_tok w has a 35% firing rate (5.7x lift), m 33%, k 22%, then a, o, t far below. A w or m in the second original position also triggers it. Top activations come from sequences like w m w ... or w w ..., and peak at or just before <DEL>. Firing rate rises with original position (highest at orig_idx 5-7) and is 22% at <DEL>. Within active steps, first-occurrence inputs are favoured (in_first=1). The predicate gets dev F1 about 0.69 and mass recall about 0.80. The misses are mostly weak activations (under 0.25 of max) in sequences without w/m/k at the start, so the feature is graded, not cleanly binary. It does not fire at the first three steps, in the copy phase, or strongly in sequences whose opening tokens are not w/m/k.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: w, m, k, a, o, t; least: c, j, f, 3) and the second original token (most: w, m, k, s, t, v; least: c, j, 3, f); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
